links.passage: Hence, regulatory requirements were put in place to ensure that irrigation water meters operate at an acceptable level of performance [10].
supporting_passages: A critical step towards improving the WUE is the ability to accurately measure the amount of water supplied to irrigators.

However, previous research undertaken in Australia showed that inaccurate flow measurement techniques, for instance using the Dethridge wheels, led to the supply of irrigation water in excess of entitlement volumes.
A study by Goulburn Water [9] showed that large Dethridge wheels operated with inaccuracies of between −18% to +3%.
The irrigation modernisation program involved the replacement of Dethridge wheels with water meters that were compliant with these regulations.
links.inference_note: The paper states accurate measurement of supplied water is critical to WUE, that inaccurate Dethridge wheel metering [9] led to over-supply beyond entitlements, and that compliant water meters [10] replaced them, so accurate flow metering is linked to delivery control and water saving.
